It contains no\nwarrior code. The language itself is documented in `redcode/`, `guide.htm` and\n`icws94-standard.txt`.\n\n## Archetypes\n\n- **Imp.** `MOV 0, 1` copies itself one cell ahead forever.\n  - Imps are very hard to kill and kill almost nothing, so on their own they mostly tie.\n  - Several imps spaced CORESIZE/n apart and executed in turn form an *imp ring* or\n    *imp spiral*, which is sturdier.\n- **Stone (bomber).** A small loop that drops bombs (DAT to kill, SPL to slow) at a\n  fixed step through the core.\n  - It is small, fast and hard to find.\n  - The choice of step matters: it decides how evenly and how fast the core gets\n    covered.\n- **Paper (replicator).** Copies itself to new places, again and again, and spawns many\n  processes.\n  - Killing one copy does not kill the warrior, so DAT bombs alone rarely beat it.\n  - \"Silk\" papers copy with `SPL`/`MOV` pairs and post-increment pointers.\n- **Scanner.** Looks for non-empty cells (`SEQ`/`SNE`/`JMZ`), then attacks what it\n  found.\n  - Typical attacks: a few bombs, a carpet of `SPL 0` bombs that stuns the target, or a\n    switch into a core clear.\n  - A scanner has to avoid detecting itself, and its speed is measured in cells per\n    cycle (0.5c, 0.66c, ...).\n- **Core clear.** Overwrites the whole core in sequence, typically with SPL first\n  (stun), then DAT (kill).\n  - Clears are used to finish off stunned opponents. They are often the last phase of a\n    scanner.\n- **Quick-scan (qscan).** A fast, unrolled scan of many cells right at the start of the\n  round.\n  - It catches an opponent before the opponent has booted or replicated.\n  - When it finds nothing, it hands over to the main warrior.\n- **Vampire.** Bombs with `JMP` \"fangs\" that redirect enemy processes into a pit that\n  makes them harmless or useful.\n- **P-space switcher.** Uses the private p-space memory, which persists between the\n  rounds of a battle, to pick a strategy in each round from earlier results. As an example, \"STP #9,#1\" stores number 9\n432-       in P-cell 1.\n433-\n434:       Since  all  P-space access is only via these two instructions, it takes\n435:       too much time and space to use P-space for working variables where they\n436:       would  be safe from the opposing warrior. P-space was made deliberately\n437-       hard to access, unlike a set of general purpose registers.\n438-\n439:       P-space can also be used for communication between  warriors  belonging\n440:       to  a  team  in multi-warrior core war. To allow communication, P-space\n441-       has to be declared as \"shared\". {"type":"text","timestamp":1794665217214,"sessionID":"ses_e25ad0914ffeL0KFkxhK36tiVU","part":{"id":"prt_1da61f85e001rnnqye36v96KpS","messageID":"msg_1da61c4c0001nBr4REBWQmmYu1","sessionID":"ses_e25ad0914ffeL0KFkxhK36tiVU","type":"text","text":"I submitted a one-shot scanner that switches to a core clear. It scores **0.489** on the sparring set over 500 rounds per opponent. The Dwarf example scores 0.181 on the same set, so it is well above the zero point. It should also land in the upper part of the reward range on the hidden hill, but that depends on how closely the hidden hill tracks the sparring set.\n\nThe submission is the 10-line warrior below; the same file is in `/app/submission.red`.\n\n```\n;redcode-94\n;name Glance\n;author me\n;assert CORESIZE==8000\nst      equ 32\nd       equ 16\n        org loop\ngate    dat    0, 0\ninc     dat    st, st\nloop    add.f  inc, sc\nsc      sne.i  100, 100+d\n        djn    loop, #243\n        mov.ab sc, gate\nclr     spl    #0, 0\n        mov    bmb, >gate\n        djn.f  clr+1, >gate\nbmb     dat    0, 11\n```\n\n**How it works:**\n- **Scan:** it compares two cells 16 apart, stepping 32 cells each time. It starts 100 cells ahead, since the opponent can't start closer than that. One pass covers the core in about 730 cycles and stops before it reaches its own code.\n- **Clear:** when it finds something, or the pass ends, it points the clear 3 cells before the target. The clear then writes DAT forward over the whole core, and the `SPL #0` gives it many processes. When the clear wraps round to its own code, it overwrites the `gate` cell, which resets the pointer to just past the code, so it never kills itself.\n\n**What I tried that scored worse:**\n- A plain bomber scored 0.31 and a replicating paper 0.25.\n- Switching between strategies using the memory that carries over between rounds dropped the score to 0.35–0.39, partly because the extra code makes the warrior a bigger target.\n- Laying a carpet of SPL bombs before the clear, or bombing each find and carrying on scanning, did worse.\n- Faster scan loops scored the same.\n- Two clears running in opposite directions, booting a copy elsewhere, decoys, and running a small bomber alongside the scanner all did worse.\n\n**Weak spots:** it loses heavily to a few sparring opponents (s21, s25, and to a lesser extent s14, s15, s17). Tiny code changes move the sparring score by about ±0.03 for no clear reason. That suggests the choices I tuned only on sparring results, like the 100-cell start and the step of 32, may not carry over fully to the hidden hill.","time":{"start":1794665216094,"end":1794665217210}}}
